ImageDescription.value: Ford Model T Runabout 1913. (This is not a standard 1913 Runabout. Its body is like that of the 1909-1912 Roadster models, with a third seat in the rear and open sides without doors. However, its windshield is supported similarly to that of the 1911 Torpedo and Open Runabouts, with support rods that extend down to the lower body panels.)

64271284.title: File:1913 Ford Model T T1 Roadster (12702957045).jpg

ImageDescription.value:
1913 Ford Model T Runabout. (This example is a bit nonstandard, with a flat rear deck instead of the usual turtledeck.)

The Ford Motor Company was established in 1903, The Model T Ford was built from 1908-1927, a few models were built before the Model T, but the T was the first mass produced car. Ford wanted to keep the price low as possible, so to increase efficiency, he was the first to use assembly line production. Ford also made use of the knock-down kit concept, so almost from the beginning, the Model T was built in many other countries as well as the US, such as England and Australia.

The first car imported to Australia was the Model A in 1904, The Model T imported from 1909. From 1925, Fords were assembled in Geelong, Australia.

The Model T slowly developed over its production life;

1909-14 T1; Flat top hood, flat cowl below the screen and gas lights. Cars from 1913 to 14 had the dog leg windscreen

1915-16 T2; had louvres in hood, contoured cowl and electric lights..

1917-23 T3; The hood tapered with a curved top, hinges moved.

1923-25 T4; Angled Screen, taller and wider at firewall.

1926-27 T5; Wire wheels, cowl now similar to Model A.

Body styles available in 1909 were; 2 door tourer, 2 door sedan, 2 door coupe, the towncar and the no door roadster

Engine; 20hp 177 Cu in

ImageDescription.value:
Ford Model T (1913) Touring Car, 4 cyl., side valves, 2892 cm3, 20 hp, max. speed 70 km/h
(Musée Automobile Reims Champagne, Reims, Marne, France)
(This car is unusual: although dated as 1913, at first glance it is of 1915–1916 style, especially the flared "cowl" behind the hood, the louvres on the hood, and the straight windshield without support rods. However, the cowl is a single smooth piece instead of three joined panels like a standard 1915–1916 cowl, and there are no side lamps beneath the windshield. Other features, such as the straight rear fenders, are of pre-1915 type, and the doors are 1913-style. The gas headlamps could be either vintage, since such headlamps were still in use on some early 1915 cars.)
At Henry Ford Memorial Day , Hamilton , NZ.
